paragraphs: The Urban Pacific Group of Companies ("Sponsor") seeks approximately $9.25 million of Opportunity Zone Joint Venture Equity, which will be used to scale the Urban Town House strategy ("UTH"), an uncommon and unique innovation of the modern build-for-rent residential development. To start in 2026, we hereby present a new UTH project in Rialto, CA with a $24.2 million estimated cost. Sponsor intends to acquire the project site upon funding of construction debt and equity. The project is zoned by-right thereby limiting risk. The Sponsor plans to develop the UTH communities to serve the "forgotten middle" of the underserved multigenerational and economic-sharing households while producing superior returns to investors.

The project, 149 W. Randall, Rialto, CA is a $24.2 million project with 48 units. At land closing, we intend to have 100% CD's in place. The project presently projects a 7.12% Untrended Yield On Cost, and an 18.57% Project IRR on a 10-Year hold basis. This strategy provides an investor the opportunity to align with seasoned developers to deliver an undersupplied rental product for a robust demographic in Southern California at strong returns while maximizing OZ tax benefits.
summary.conclusion: For investors, UTH presents a lucrative opportunity to tap into a market with strong demand and potential for steady returns.

data.summary: The market demonstrates a severe lack of purpose-built 5-bedroom rental product. Current supply is limited to traditional multi-family 3-bedroom units or single-family home conversions, which lack the professional management and efficiency of the UTH model. Average occupancy for modern comparables in the region sits at 93%.

paragraphs: Urban Pacific Group of Companies is a California-based real estate investment and development firm founded in 2000 by Scott Choppin. The firm is the innovator of the Urban Town House (UTH) housing model, which pairs private capital with middle-income multigenerational rental housing throughout California and the Western U.S.

Urban Pacific focuses on workforce rental housing communities for the "forgotten middle"—multigenerational and economic-sharing households underserved by traditional multifamily supply. The sponsor self-performs construction across its UTH developments, bringing cost certainty and transparency to each project.

teamMembers.title: CEO & Founder
teamMembers.background: Scott Choppin founded Urban Pacific in 2000 and pioneered the Urban Town House (UTH) strategy—five-bedroom, four-bathroom build-for-rent townhomes designed for multigenerational and economic-sharing households. He has spent the last eight years refining the UTH concept and scaling the model across Southern California, with the sponsor self-performing construction to maintain cost certainty across its development pipeline.
